Compare Subsequence Patterns Between Groups

Source: R/sequence_compare.R
sequence_compare.Rd

sequence_compare() compares how often short subsequences occur in two or more groups of sequences. For each pattern length in sub it counts every k-gram (a run of k consecutive states, such as "A->B->C") in each group, keeps the patterns that are frequent enough in every group, and returns a net_sequence_comparison whose pattern table has one row per pattern with its count, proportion and standardised residual in each group and, optionally, a permutation or chi-square test of whether its frequency differs between the groups. It takes a grouped network, a single network or wide sequences with a grouping.

A residual says how far a group's count of a pattern lies from the count expected if pattern and group were independent, in approximately standard-normal units (Haberman, 1973); a positive value means the pattern is more frequent in that group than independence predicts. The p-values are adjusted across every pattern tested. The permutation test treats the sequence as the unit, while the chi-square test treats every occurrence as independent, which overstates the evidence when occurrences within a sequence depend on each other (see Details). Patterns of different lengths overlap (each 3-gram contains two 2-grams), so their tests are not independent of each other. sequence_patterns() with group asks the related question of whether a pattern is present in more sequences of one group.

Usage

sequence_compare(
  x,
  group = NULL,
  sub = 3:5,
  min_freq = 5L,
  test = c("permutation", "chisq", "none"),
  iter = 1000L,
  adjust = "fdr"
)

# S3 method for class 'net_sequence_comparison'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_sequence_comparison'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_sequence_comparison'
plot(
  x,
  top_n = 10L,
  style = c("auto", "pyramid", "heatmap"),
  sort = c("statistic", "frequency"),
  alpha = 0.05,
  show_residuals = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

The sequences: a netobject_group (from build_network() with group, or from a clustering), whose groups are compared; a netobject, tna model or cograph_network built from sequences; a wide data frame with one row per sequence and one column per position, whose position columns are named as a numbered run, as in build_network() (any column beside them other than the group column raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input); or a character matrix with one row per sequence and one column per position, whatever its column names. A numeric or logical matrix of only 0 and 1, and one-hot or association networks, raise nestimate_bad_input. Every input except a netobject_group needs group. For the print() and plot() methods: a net_sequence_comparison.

group

The group of each sequence: the name of a column of a data frame or matrix x (that column is then not read as a position), or a vector with one label per sequence. Ignored for a netobject_group; required otherwise. At least two groups are needed. Default NULL.

sub

The pattern lengths to count, positive whole numbers. Lengths longer than the sequences are dropped, and an error is raised when none remains. Default 3:5.

min_freq

The smallest count a pattern must reach in every group to be kept, a positive whole number; when no pattern of any length reaches it, an error is raised. Default 5.

test

The inference: "permutation" (default), "chisq" or "none"; see Details.

iter

The number of permutations for test = "permutation", a positive whole number; ignored otherwise. Default 1000.

adjust

The p-value adjustment, any method of stats::p.adjust() ("holm", "hochberg", "hommel", "bonferroni", "BH", "BY", "fdr" or "none"). Default "fdr" (Benjamini-Hochberg).

...

Not used.

object

For the summary() method: a net_sequence_comparison.

top_n

For plot(): the number of patterns drawn, the first ones after ranking by sort. Default 10.

style

For plot(): "auto" (default) draws the back-to-back pyramid for exactly 2 groups and the heatmap for any other number; "pyramid" and "heatmap" force one. "pyramid" with other than 2 groups raises an error.

sort

For plot(): how to pick and order the patterns. "statistic" (default) ranks them by the absolute effect size after a permutation test, by the chi-square statistic after a chi-square test, and by the largest absolute residual without a test. "frequency" ranks them by their total count across the groups.

alpha

For the pyramid: the significance level for the p-value labels. Patterns with p_value < alpha are starred and drawn in bold dark text, the rest in plain grey. Default 0.05. The heatmap and a comparison without a test ignore it.

show_residuals

For the pyramid: whether to print each bar's standardised residual inside it. Default FALSE. The heatmap always prints the residuals.

Value

A net_sequence_comparison object. print() shows the numbers of patterns and groups, the settings and the first 10 rows of the pattern table, and returns its input invisibly; summary() returns the pattern table, a data frame with one row per pattern; plot() draws the residuals of the top patterns (see Plot styles). The object holds:

patterns

The pattern table, one row per k-gram kept. Always: pattern, length, and per group freq_<group> (the count), prop_<group> (the count as a share of all k-grams of that length in the group, rare ones included) and resid_<group> (the standardised residual). With test = "permutation" also effect_size and p_value; with test = "chisq", statistic and p_value. The p-values are adjusted. Rows are ordered by ascending p_value (ties by the larger absolute effect size, or the larger statistic) when a test was run, and by descending largest absolute residual otherwise.

groups

The group names, sorted.

n_patterns

The number of rows of the pattern table: the patterns that reach min_freq in every group.

params

The settings used: sub (after dropping lengths longer than the sequences), min_freq, test, iter and adjust.

Details

The standardised residuals come from the 2 x G table of the pattern's counts against the counts of all other k-grams of the same length in each group, with the formula (o - e) / sqrt(e * (1 - r/N) * (1 - c/N)). They are always computed, whatever test is. A k-gram that spans a missing position is not counted.

test chooses the inference:

"permutation"

Shuffles the group labels across sequences iter times and recomputes, for each pattern, the Euclidean norm of its row of differences between observed and expected counts in the patterns-by-groups table of the patterns kept at that length (expected under independence). It asks whether the pattern's distribution is associated with group membership at the level of the sequence, which respects the sequence as the unit of analysis but has little power when there are few sequences. The p-value is (b + 1) / (iter + 1), where b counts the permutations with a statistic at least as large as the observed one, so it cannot fall below 1 / (iter + 1). The effect size is the observed statistic minus the mean of the permuted ones, divided by their standard deviation (taken as 1 when the permuted statistics do not vary; with iter = 1 the effect size is NA, since at least two permutations are needed). The shuffles use R's random number generator: call base::set.seed() first for reproducible p-values.

"chisq"

Runs stats::chisq.test() on each pattern's 2 x G table (with Yates' continuity correction when there are two groups). It asks whether the groups' streams of k-grams produce the pattern at different rates, treating every occurrence as an independent event: it is fast and has power with few sequences, but the independence it assumes is optimistic when sequences are strongly autocorrelated.

"none"

No test; the counts, proportions and residuals only.

The p-values are adjusted once across all patterns of all lengths, with stats::p.adjust().

Plot styles

plot() draws the standardised residuals of the top top_n patterns, prints the plot and returns the ggplot invisibly (NULL, with a message, when there are no patterns). style = "auto" (the default) picks the style from the number of groups:

"pyramid"

Back-to-back bars of each pattern's proportion in the two groups, each bar shaded by that group's standardised residual (the colour saturates at plus or minus 3), with the (adjusted) p-value in the gap between the bars when a test was run. Needs exactly 2 groups.

"heatmap"

One tile per pattern and group, coloured by the standardised residual (the colour saturates at plus or minus 3) and labelled with its value. Works for any number of groups.

The residuals are filled whatever test was chosen, so both styles work after test = "none".

References

Haberman, S. J. (1973). The analysis of residuals in cross-classified tables. Biometrics, 29(1), 205–220. (standardised residuals)

Benjamini, Y. & Hochberg, Y. (1995). Controlling the false discovery rate. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society B, 57(1), 289–300. (the default adjust = "fdr")

Examples

set.seed(1)
seqs <- data.frame(
  V1 = sample(LETTERS[1:4], 60, TRUE),
  V2 = sample(LETTERS[1:4], 60, TRUE),
  V3 = sample(LETTERS[1:4], 60, TRUE),
  V4 = sample(LETTERS[1:4], 60, TRUE)
)
grp <- rep(c("X", "Y"), 30)
net <- build_network(seqs, method = "relative")
res <- sequence_compare(net, group = grp, sub = 2:3, test = "chisq")
